sections.h2: Where is the Edmonson County Clerk's office?
sections.html:
The Edmonson County Clerk works from 108 N. Main Street in Brownsville, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 830, Brownsville, KY 42210. The phone number is 270-597-2624. Hours vary by day:

  • Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday: 8 in the morning until 4 in the afternoon
  • Thursday and Saturday: mornings only, closing at noon
  • Friday: 8 until 5

Saturday morning hours help sellers who work weekdays. Brownsville holds the courthouse and is the one incorporated city in Edmonson County, so every deed for a house in the county, wherever it sits, comes to this one counter.

sections.h2: How far back do Edmonson County land records go?
sections.html:
The clerk keeps most documents at the courthouse from 1840 to the present, and indexes reach back to 1840 for most document types. Images of nearly every instrument filed since January 1986 are online. All deeds from the county's start are online, and mortgage images are online from 1986 forward. Veteran discharge records are not made available, for security reasons.

Online records include deeds, mortgages, mechanics liens, powers of attorney, wills, assignments, releases, tax liens and delinquent property taxes. That depth lets a seller or a title agent trace ownership of an old farm parcel without a trip to the courthouse.

sections.h2: What are the posted Edmonson County recording fees?
sections.html:
The clerk posts a minimum fee table, and a deed is $50. A mortgage is $80, and a full or partial release of mortgage is $46. The posted table is headed as a list of minimum fees, so confirm the total for a long document with the clerk.

Edmonson County recording fees, selected items (source: Edmonson County Clerk, Records page)

sections.h2: Can I e-record or search records online in Edmonson County?
sections.html:
The clerk lists four e-recording services: Hopdox, CSC, Simplifile and ePN. Ask your closing agent whether they will submit electronically instead of carrying paper to the counter. The office runs its records on Software Management's system and offers an eCCLIX search.

Private citizens who live in the county can search Edmonson County records for personal reasons at no charge, limited to five searches a day. Commercial users pay a subscription. All public records can be viewed in the clerk's office free of charge.

sections.h2: What is DOCALERT and why would a homeowner sign up?
sections.html:
DOCALERT is a free email service that the clerk's office offers with Software Management, LLC. You register with a name and an email address, and the service sends an alert whenever a mortgage or deed under that name is recorded in Edmonson County. The point is fraud protection. A sudden filing that you did not sign would show up in your inbox quickly.

Sellers who own several parcels or who have inherited land held in a relative's name may want to register every name tied to the property, so a new filing does not go unseen.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax does an Edmonson County seller pay?
sections.html:
The state taxes the grantor $0.50 per $500 slice of value, with any partial slice counted whole, and the clerk takes payment before recording. A deed at the county's typical home value of $160,300 covers 321 slices, so the bill is $160.50. Value means the full consideration paid, including liens, or the fair market value for a gift or a deed with nominal consideration.

KRS 142.050 exempts foreclosure deeds, correction deeds, divorce transfers between spouses and nominal-value family deeds from parent to child or grandparent to grandchild. The clerk keeps 5 percent and forwards the balance to the county treasurer every three months.

sections.h2: When are Edmonson County tax bills due, and where do they go after April 15?
sections.html:
The Sheriff's Office at 110 Jackson Street collects it. Bills are mailed on October 30, and anyone without one by November 15 should call 270-597-2157 for a duplicate. Payment through November 30 earns a 2 percent discount, December 1 to 31 is the base amount, January adds 5 percent and February 1 on adds 21 percent. Everything must be paid by April 15.

After that date the bill sits with the County Clerk as a certificate of delinquency. In 2026 the clerk advertised the 2025 delinquent real property bills on August 19 and set the sale for September 15 at 11:00 a.m., with registration closing September 4 and a 25 percent deposit required of bidders. Taxpayers could pay the clerk in full any time before the sale, and the notice said payments received after the sale would be returned.

sections.h2: Who values property in Edmonson County?
sections.html:
The Property Valuation Administrator at 110 E. Main Cross Street in Brownsville assesses all property in the county for the state, the county and other districts. Reach the office at 270-597-2381. Doors are open Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday from 7:30 until 4:30, and Thursday and Saturday mornings until noon.

Owners who disagree with a value must have a conference with the PVA during the May inspection period, then file with the clerk by the next workday after it closes. Homeowners 65 or older, or totally disabled, can apply to the PVA for the $49,100 homestead exemption that applies for 2025 and 2026.

sections.h2: What else does the Edmonson County Clerk's office do besides deeds?
sections.html:
The same counter serves drivers and voters. The clerk's site links to vehicle registration renewal, driver license renewal through Drive.ky.gov, voter registration, a lookup of vehicle tax paid last year by VIN, and bridge toll payments through River Link. Two of those matter to a seller: the Find and View Delinquent Taxes page and the Find and View Land Records page, which opens the eCCLIX search.

Call 270-597-2624 before you go, since Thursday and Saturday close at noon.

sections.h2: What is Edmonson County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Edmonson County was formed on January 12, 1825 from parts of Grayson, Hart and Warren counties and is named for Captain John Edmonson, killed at the Battle of Frenchtown in 1813. A courthouse built in 1873 replaced an earlier building whose floor collapsed. The county covers 308 square miles, has Mammoth Cave National Park within it, is dry, and sits in the Bowling Green metropolitan area.

The population was 12,126 in 2020 and is estimated at 12,749 for July 2025, up 5.1 percent. QuickFacts lists 6,533 housing units, and 80.1 percent of households own. Homes typically value $160,300 and rent typically runs $778. One resident in five, 20.9 percent, is past 65, so the homestead exemption applies to many owners.

faqs.q: What is the Edmonson County Clerk's phone number?
faqs.a: 270-597-2624. The office is at 108 N. Main Street in Brownsville and is open Saturday mornings as well as weekdays.

faqs.q: What is the clerk's minimum fee for a deed in Edmonson County?
faqs.a: The clerk's posted minimum fee for a deed is $50. A deed of correction is $46, and a mortgage is $80.

faqs.q: Are Edmonson County deeds available online?
faqs.a: Yes. All deeds from the county's inception are online, and images of most instruments filed since January 1986 are online too. Mortgage images are online from 1986.

faqs.q: Can I pay a delinquent Edmonson County tax bill after the sheriff's deadline?
faqs.a: Yes, through the County Clerk. Pay in full before the tax sale date the clerk advertises, since payments received after a sale are returned.

faqs.q: Does Edmonson County have more than one city?
faqs.a: No. Brownsville, the courthouse town, is the one municipality, so county offices handle nearly every tax question.
